newsitem.title: USA: NY PRECIOUS METALS MOSTLY LOWER AFTER U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: NY PRECIOUS METALS MOSTLY LOWER AFTER U.S. DATA.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were mixed mostly lower early Wednesday, retreating from a higher opening, after the latest U.S. economic data allowed U.S. bonds and stocks to recover strongly.

U.S. July retail sales rose 0.6 percent, largely matching expectations, while the U.S. July PPI fell 0.1 pct, the seventh consecutive monthly decline, erasing the latest bout of inflation fears which had contributed to the past week's sharp downward correction in bonds and stocks.
As a result, gold prices slipped, after nervousness about a sharp correction in the stock market had provided some support for gold in the past week.
COMEX December gold was down 20 cents at $330.60 an ounce after the first hour of trade, after seeing an early high at $332.90.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $326.10/60 an ounce, compared to the London Wednesday morning fix at $328.60 and $324.80 in New York late Tuesday.

Implied gold lease rates rose sharply again Wednesday, to 2.29 pct for one month from 1.93 pct Tuesday, and to 2.26 percent for one year from 2.20 pct, suggesting funds and producers may be borrowing again to fund short positions and hedges, with gold back near the top of its range of the past month around $330.00 in the spot market.
COMEX September silver was up 1.0 cent at $4.435 an ounce, after seeing an early high at $4.465.
NYMEX October platinum was off $4.50 at $430.50, while NYMEX September palladium was down $2.00 to $204.50.
